name: Tunisian Harissa Coconut Beef Meatballs
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Both signature ingredients, harissa-paste and coconut-milk-canned, are already tracked commodities, which is rare for a North African dish. One skillet of sauce, meatballs simmer in it. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated. | HARVEST: Source title is 'Creamy Coconut Harissa Beef Meatballs'.
intro_html: Harissa and coconut milk should not work together, and then you taste it. The harissa brings smoke and heat, the coconut milk rounds it off, and beef meatballs simmer right in the sauce so they soak up both. It is a weeknight cook that eats like something you planned for days. Each bowl carries {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost).
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Harissa Paste, 1.25 cups: ~$5.25. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 10oz jars.
Rice, 4 cups dry: ~$0.86. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Pantry seasonings (garam masala, salt, black pepper): ~$0.51. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $38.71 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.76 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $44.51 across 14 servings, roughly $3.18 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $14.47 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $58.98. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost), which is remarkable for a dish with this much going on. Ground beef and rice do the heavy lifting, and the harissa jar carries you through several batches.
shop_smart: Harissa paste looks expensive on the shelf and cheap on the plate. One jar seasons multiple batches and it keeps for months in the fridge after opening.
Ground beef is the biggest line. Watch for the club size packs, break them down into batch sized portions the day you get home, and freeze what you are not cooking.
Canned coconut milk is a pantry staple worth buying several of when it is on promotion. It does not spoil and it turns up in a lot of recipes.
One bunch of cilantro covers both the meatball mix and the garnish. Stand it stems down in a glass of water in the fridge and it will hold for a week.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Grate or very finely chop about a third of the onion and mix it into the ground beef with half the garlic, a good handful of chopped cilantro, the garam masala, salt, and pepper.
Roll the mixture into meatballs of a consistent size. Uniform meatballs cook evenly and portion evenly, which matters more here than looks.
Sear the meatballs in the vegetable oil in batches, turning to brown them on several sides. They do not need to cook through yet.
Chop the remaining onion and cook it in the same pot until soft, then add the rest of the garlic for a minute.
Stir in the harissa paste and let it fry for a minute, then pour in the coconut milk and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Return the meatballs, cover, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until they are cooked through and the sauce has thickened around them.
Cook the rice separately and scatter the remaining cilantro over the top before portioning.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Count the meatballs out evenly first, then spoon the same weight of sauce over each, and give every container the same weight of rice. Each bowl lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Mix ground beef with grated onion, garlic, cilantro, and spices and roll into meatballs.
Sear the meatballs in oil in batches until browned on several sides.
Soften the remaining onion and garlic, then fry the harissa paste.
Add coconut milk, return the meatballs, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes.
Cook the rice and portion meatballs, sauce, and rice into 14 containers.
